$comment: Mach-O EXECUTABLE (MH_EXECUTE) for x86_64 Darwin/macOS. Second Mach-O schema (plan 14 LK3 cycle 2, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/macho.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Differs from `macho64-x86_64-darwin.format.json` (the MH_OBJECT schema) in: `macho.filetype = 2` (MH_EXECUTE); `macho.flags` includes MH_PIE (0x200000) + MH_NOUNDEFS (0x1) + MH_DYLDLINK (0x4) + MH_TWOLEVEL (0x80) = 0x200085 (modern macOS exec convention); sections carry `virtualAddress` (loaded at ImageBase + offset); top-level `entryPoint` names the LC_MAIN entry-function symbol; new `image` block carries __PAGEZERO size + LC_LOAD_DYLINKER path + LC_LOAD_DYLIB list.
$absentKeyRationaleComment: Machine-read by tests/link/test_object_format_family_symmetry.cpp: every root key a SIBLING of this format declares and this file does not must appear below with a non-empty reason, and every entry below must correspond to a real absence. Both directions fail loud, so this table can neither be skipped nor rot after a gap is closed.

$absentKeyRationale.librarySynthesis: DELIBERATE, and argued at length in this file's own `$remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment` row (4): `librarySynthesis` is the vehicle for the C11 `<threads.h>` shim, and it has NO CONSUMER on this format -- the shim is a TLS-shaped facility and this format ships no `tlsAccess` either (row 1), while the staged upstream sqlite corpus uses pthread directly. Declaring it would advertise a capability nothing exercises and no leg witnesses.
$absentKeyRationale.tlsAccess: DELIBERATE, and PINNED BY A NAMED TEST rather than merely intended -- tests/link/test_linker.cpp `Linker.TdataItemOnNonOptedInFormatsRejectsAtAcceptsGate` asserts ASSERT_FALSE(acceptsDataSection(Tdata)) (and the same for Tbss) against THIS format by name, so declaring `tlsAccess` here turns that test red. Argued in this file's `$remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment` row (1): it is no longer a runtime-witness problem (the Rosetta leg exists) but a NO-CONSUMER one -- MEASURED, the staged upstream `sqlite3.c` and `shell.c` contain ZERO `_Thread_local`/`__thread`/`thread_local` occurrences. A `_Thread_local` TU on this format walls loud (`K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport ... declares no tlsAccess block`), which is the correct outcome, not a gap.

$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: Mach-O CAN express a per-program stack reserve -- `LC_MAIN.stacksize` is a genuine equivalent of the PE optional header's SizeOfStackReserve -- but NO DSS walker arm writes it yet, so this schema deliberately declares no `stackReserveControl` and a request is REFUSED. Shipping the capability without the walker would let a request be accepted and silently dropped; declaring the gap keeps it VISIBLE. TRACKED as [[D-LK-MACHO-STACK-RESERVE-LC-MAIN]] -- and that registry row is the point: unlike the other three reason verbs (`runtime-controlled`, `loader-ignores-field`, `no-image-field`), which state PERMANENT facts about a platform, this one names a gap that is OURS and is CLOSABLE, so it carries a trigger and defined closing work in the backlog rather than only a well-written comment (the comment tells whoever HITS it; the row is what keeps it from being forgotten). When the macho walker arm lands, this key is replaced by a `stackReserveControl` block with a `macho-lc-main` vehicle and this format moves to the positive side of the linker gate's coverage sweep.
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit linux/darwin are LP64 (int 32, long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c long binds I64 here. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: Apple's C ABI prefixes EVERY C symbol with exactly ONE leading underscore, on both 32- and 64-bit Mach-O -- the rule has no bitness axis and no per-arch axis (the arm64 and x86_64 slices of the universal libSystem decorate identically), which is why it is declared per FORMAT and not per target. EVIDENCE, EACH LABELLED. MEASURED-BY-EXECUTION (recorded TF-C113, the macOS cross-build arc): a Windows host cross-emitted a mach-o arm64 binary whose only process-exit path is the `_exit` import, and it RAN on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac and exited correctly -- an undecorated `exit` would have been an unresolved dyld bind, not a cosmetic difference. MEASURED (recorded TF-C121): libSystem's x86_64 slice exports BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64`, i.e. the C identifier `fstat` reaches the linker as `_fstat`. NOT RE-MEASURED THIS CYCLE, stated rather than buried: the Mac is a personal machine and was not declared reachable, so nothing here rests on a probe taken today. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: macOS x86_64 generic LSB-first bit-field allocation == gnu_packed (Apple does not diverge from generic AAPCS64 on bit-field packing). Byte-ABI-exact to clang. See macho64-x86_64-darwin for the divergence-list rationale.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: macOS x86_64 `long double` is the x87 80-bit extended format stored 16/16 (the SysV-x86_64 rule; Apple's x86_64 ABI follows SysV here). The axis resolves the c row to F80 — declarations/layout/sizeof work; VALUE arithmetic walls loud until D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE-X87-ARITH lands.
$entryPointComment: Empty defaults to module.functions[0] (cycle-2 convention). LC_MAIN.entryoff is computed as (entry_function_offset_in_.text) — relative to the __TEXT segment start, NOT to file offset.
$externCallDispatchComment: DIRECT-PLT (corrected from the original mislabel). Mach-O resolves imports through a per-extern __stubs entry: the linker points each extern symbol's VA at its __stubs STUB (code) — see `symbolVa[extern] = stubVa` in macho.cpp — and the stub does the __got indirection internally (x86_64 `FF 25 disp32` jmp through the __got slot; ARM64 ADRP+LDR+BR x16). The call site is therefore a PLAIN DIRECT call (x86_64 `E8 disp32`, ARM64 `BL`) to the stub — byte-identical in shape to an intra-module call — NOT an `FF 15`-through-the-stub deref (that would dereference the stub's CODE bytes as a function pointer → SIGSEGV). This is the SAME direct-plt model ELF uses, and it matches what the trampoline + MIR→LIR `lowerCall` emit. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$entryClusterDischargedComment: ★ THE D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-EXIT DEFERRAL IS DISCHARGED HERE — this key pair REPLACES the `$processExitDeferredComment` that stood in this slot. That comment posed the choice as (a) by-name-import of libSystem `_exit` vs (b) the raw BSD syscall 0x2000001, deferred the answer 'to the first Mach-O runnable-binary trigger', and closed by calling the resulting silent skip 'intentional, not a defect'. BOTH halves are now obsolete. THE CHOICE WAS MADE AND SHIPPED: the arm64 sibling took option (a) and is the RUNTIME-WITNESSED leg (a DSS-built mach-o exec ran on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac); Apple declares BSD syscall numbers unstable across macOS versions, and libSystem is loaded by every macOS process anyway, which is what settled (a) over (b). ★ SAY THE EVIDENCE GRADE PLAINLY, BECAUSE THIS FILE HOLDS ITSELF TO A STRICTER ONE TWELVE LINES DOWN. The runtime witness is arm64's; there is NO x86_64 macOS witness in this project (the operator's Mac is Apple Silicon), so the entry cluster shipped HERE is INFERRED, not measured: `_exit` is the same libSystem symbol under the same format-kind mangling rule, and `sysv_amd64` derives from the abi_catalog x86_64+MachO row plus the same-named convention on x86_64.target.json. An earlier wording said 'the trigger the deferral waited for has already fired for this format family', which reads as though the x86_64 cluster inherited the arm64 run — it did not. What actually forces the cluster to ship regardless is the new validate() rule: an MH_EXECUTE schema declaring no `processExit` is now rejected at config load, so 'omit until witnessed' (the stance `$remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment` still takes for the data sections) is not an available option here. Ship it INFERRED and say so, rather than let two evidentiary standards sit unremarked in one file. AND THE SILENT SKIP IS NO LONGER THE PROJECT'S POSITION: `format.processExit().has_value()` returning false on an EXEC-flavored format means the emitted image's entry points straight at the user's `main` with no exit spine — a program that falls off the end of `main` into whatever follows it, produced with NO diagnostic. That is a silent-miscompile shape, and this cycle makes it fail LOUD instead. A format that claims MH_EXECUTE must therefore declare its exit spine; this file now does. NOTE the deliberate NON-symmetry with the arm64 sibling: only the ENTRY CLUSTER is being brought over. Everything else this file omits stays omitted on purpose — see $remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment below, which names the test that pins each one.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the ROLE -> IMAGE table, and the SINGLE OWNER of 'which image plays which runtime role' for this format. The spine blocks below name a ROLE and the loader resolves it here; each block's resolved path is a DERIVED copy and ObjectFormatData::validate() re-checks the pair, so the two cannot drift. * ON DARWIN ONE IMAGE GENUINELY PLAYS SEVERAL ROLES -- libSystem.B.dylib is both the C library and the pthread primitive provider -- and expressing that is exactly what a role TABLE does and a single per-format CRT string cannot: on pe64 the synthesis vehicle's image (kernel32.dll) is NOT the C library, while here it IS, so any scheme that carried one image per format would be silently wrong on one of the two. The table PERMITS sameness without ASSERTING it. * No unwindPersonality row: Mach-O declares no personality block yet, and validate() REFUSES a row nothing names rather than letting a stale image sit here unread. * importLibraryPath used to be spelled inside processExit; the value is unchanged and must still appear in image.loadDylibs so dyld can resolve it. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this row and processExit refuses the format AT LOAD, naming this file.
$entryVerbsComment: UCRT-P4 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE): the program-entry materialization VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE -- what it is able to hand a program entry before calling it. * THE ACCEPTED ENTRY SET IS AN INTERSECTION, AND THIS FILE OWNS ONLY HALF OF IT. This key used to be `entryShapes` -- full { returns, params, materialization } rows -- which made the accepted SIGNATURES a format fact. They are not one: `int wmain(int, wchar_t**)` is a C spelling, and a linker format has no opinion on how a source language spells an entry, only on what it can hand one. So the signatures moved to their single owner, the language file's `entryFunctions` mapping (src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json), which declares each name->signature->verb; this key declares the VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE. A defined function is a program-entry candidate iff its name matches a declared language row, its signature matches that row, and that row's verb appears HERE. C23 3.4.1 requires an implementation to DOCUMENT its implementation-defined choices, so the documentation artifact is the PAIR of comments -- this one and $entryFunctionsComment -- each naming the other. Reading either alone tells you less than the truth. * THE VERBS ARE DECLARED EVEN THOUGH THIS FORMAT DECLARES NO processArgs BLOCK, and the two are not in conflict: a verb says WHICH arguments the entry needs, processArgs.mechanism says HOW this format obtains them, and on Mach-O the answer to HOW is "dyld already did it" -- LC_MAIN is CALLED with argc/argv/envp/apple in the argument registers before any DSS code runs, so the trampoline passes them through untouched. An absent processArgs is a real ANSWER here, not an omission. * DARWIN PASSES FOUR VALUES, (argc, argv, envp, apple), AND THAT IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE ARGUMENT FOR THE WHOLE DESIGN BEING DECLARED DATA: an arity check in shared substrate cannot express a platform whose entry takes four. It also points at the LONG-TERM CLOSURE of the residual `.o` gap. Because dyld (and, on ELF, glibc's __libc_start_main) puts envp in the argument register BEFORE any DSS code runs, the envp materialization on these formats is PASS-THROUGH -- nothing to emit. So a 3-parameter language row with an `argc-argv-envp` verb, declared on the formats whose loader already supplies it, would make the one case no tier can detect (an entry arriving from a foreign .o, whose C signature is simply not in the input) HARMLESS instead of faulting. That is a SUPERSET MATERIALIZATION and it is not implemented: it is gated on a RUN WITNESS, which is the same reason the third and fourth parameters are absent from this file today. A shape declared without a run witness is a claim this file is not entitled to make (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE). * `argc-wargv` is absent because nothing on this platform produces a wide argument vector, which is why `wmain` is not a program entry here. * `none` is the verb `int main(void)` needs; declaring it is an ANSWER, not an omission. * RED-ON-DISABLE: drop "argc-argv" from this list and every example whose entry is `main(int, char**)` becomes unresolvable on this format -- the language's argc-argv row no longer survives the intersection, so the program has no entry candidate at all and the build is REFUSED naming this key. Empty the list entirely and the format is refused AT LOAD (exec-flavored <-> non-empty entryVerbs is pinned in both directions), because the engine reads this emptiness as "this format starts no program".
$processExitComment: STDIO-FLUSH-AT-EXIT / D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-EXIT: the macOS runnable-binary exit terminates via the C-standard `exit(3)` — which flushes line-/full-buffered stdio + runs `atexit` handlers before the process dies (returning from `main` is equivalent to calling `exit(3)`). importMangledName `_exit` is the MACH-O SYMBOL for the C function `exit`, NOT the non-flushing POSIX `_exit(2)`: Apple's C ABI prefixes every C symbol with ONE leading underscore, and that rule is keyed on the FORMAT rather than the CPU -- it is this file's own `cSymbolDecoration` key (scheme `leading-underscore`) since TF-C122, where it replaced a C++ table keyed on the format kind -- so the x86_64 slice of libSystem exports the flushing `exit(3)` under exactly the name the arm64 slice does. (The POSIX `_exit(2)` is a DIFFERENT symbol, `__exit` — two underscores.) importLibraryPath is the SAME `/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib` as the arm64 sibling and that is not a copied arch claim: the dylib is UNIVERSAL, and which slice of it this image binds against is decided by `macho.cputype` below. The trampoline places the name VERBATIM into the synthetic ExternImport (entry_trampoline.cpp does not re-mangle a processExit import), moves the user fn's return value (sysv_amd64 returnGprs[0]=rax) into argGprs[0]=rdi — a REAL `mov` here, UNLIKE the arm64 arm where the same step is a no-op x0->x0 emitted only for ABI uniformity — then makes a DIRECT call to the `_exit` __stubs entry (externCallDispatch=direct-plt above; the x86_64 stub is the 6-byte `FF 25 disp32` jmp through its __got slot, `emitX86_64MachoStub` at src/link/format/macho.cpp:301). importLibraryPath must also appear in image.loadDylibs so dyld can resolve it — it already does. Uniform with elf (libc `exit`) + pe (kernel32 `ExitProcess`, msvcrt DLL-detach flush): all four exec formats terminate through a stdio-flushing libc-level primitive.
$runnableCliClusterComment: ★ 2026-08-05 — THE FOUR KEYS BELOW (+ the three `sections[]` rows + `image.codeSignature`) WERE ADDED TOGETHER AS THE MINIMUM SUFFICIENT SET FOR A RUNNABLE macOS-x86_64 CLI, AND THE SET IS EMPIRICAL, NOT A CLONE OF THE arm64 SIBLING. Method: add one key, re-probe, read the NEXT wall, repeat — because declaring a capability with no consumer is itself a bar violation. THE MEASURED LADDER, every rung run through the real CLI from the repo root against `--target x86_64:macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec`: (0) `int main(void){return 42;}` was ALREADY rc=0 before any of this. (1) `--project` with artifactProfile `cli` failed `error[D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch] object format 'macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec' serves no artifact profiles` => `artifactProfiles`. (2) `#include <stdio.h>` + printf failed `error[K_FormatLacksImportSupport] ... extern DATA import '___stdinp' ... declares no 'dataImportBinding' model` => `dataImportBinding`. (3) it then failed `error[K_NoMatchingObjectFormat] ... section=rodata ... does not advertise that section` => `supportedDataSections` rodata + the `__TEXT,__const` row. (4) `const char msg[]="x"; int g=7; int b;` then walled on `section=data`, and after that on `section=bss` => the `data`/`bss` opt-ins + their `__DATA` rows. (5) a const function-pointer table (`static fn_t const table[2] = {alpha,beta};` + `int *const px=&x;`) walled on `section=relro` => the `relro` opt-in (NO separate row — the exec walker FOLDS relro into `__DATA,__data`, the same decision the arm64 sibling records). After (5) the whole ladder is rc=0, INCLUDING a `<stdio.h>`+`snprintf` TU, which independently corroborates the sibling cycle that shipped `snprintf` on macho rather than contradicting it. ★ WHAT IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* HERE, because the probe said so rather than because the sibling lacks it: `tlsAccess` + the `tdata`/`tbss`/`tvars` rows. A `_Thread_local` TU DOES still wall loud here (`error[K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport] ... object format declares no tlsAccess block`) — that is the correct behaviour, not a gap to paper over, because MEASURED 2026-08-05 the sqlite corpus does not need it: `grep -c -E '_Thread_local|__thread|thread_local'` over the staged upstream `sqlite3.c` AND `shell.c` returns 0 and 0. TLS on this format therefore has no consumer today and stays unshipped until one exists (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, and `Linker.TdataItemOnNonOptedInFormatsRejectsAtAcceptsGate` still pins the tdata/tbss absence on this exact format name — it was NOT weakened by this cycle).
$supportedDataSectionsComment: The exec data-section opt-in set — the LINKER's pre-walker gate reads THIS (a generic set-membership with zero format-name branches; the same field ELF + PE exec formats declare), and the `sections[]` rows below tell the WALKER where each kind lands. ★ THE TWO KEYS MUST MOVE TOGETHER, and the reason is sharper than 'they should agree': MEASURED 2026-08-05, opting into `rodata` WITHOUT its `sections[]` row does NOT fail loud — `macho::encodeExecDynamic`'s `hasConst && secConst == nullptr` guard (src/link/format/macho.cpp:2753) is a bare `return {}` with NO diagnostic, so the caller reports the generic `error[K_ImageEmpty] ... the walker returned success with no output` and the actual cause (a missing config row) is never named. Its `hasData`/`hasBss` siblings ten lines below DO emit a `K_NoMatchingObjectFormat` naming the missing row — so this is a one-arm asymmetry, not the design. Reported for anchoring; `AsmSubstrate.ShippedExecFormatsRodataSectionPerWalkerArm` now pins BOTH halves of the pair across every shipped exec format so the shipped configs cannot drift into it. Per-kind: `rodata` -> `__TEXT,__const` (folded into the R+X __TEXT segment, S_REGULAR, no write attr — W^X preserved), `data` -> `__DATA,__data`, `bss` -> `__DATA,__bss` (S_ZEROFILL), `relro` -> NO row of its own: the MH_EXECUTE walker folds a const-with-load-time-relocations item into the writable `__DATA,__data` and dyld rebases the slot via the __DATA rebase-opcode stream (D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE — the identical decision the arm64 sibling documents, and its `$relroExecComment` is the long form). `tdata`/`tbss` are ABSENT on purpose — see $runnableCliClusterComment.
$dataImportBindingComment: D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT: extern library DATA objects (Darwin `#define stdout __stdoutp` — a true extern DATA symbol with no accessor function, and the very first thing any `#include <stdio.h>` TU trips over) bind via Mach-O `__got` NON-LAZY POINTERS. Same verb + same mechanism as the arm64 sibling, and that is NOT a copied arch claim: `got-indirect` is the PIE-native model and both Darwin exec schemas set MH_PIE, while the __got slot infrastructure this extends is already present in the x86_64 image (MEASURED — the pre-cycle baseline binary carries `__DATA_CONST,__got` because the function-import stubs jump THROUGH it; this extends the same slots to DATA). The linker binds `symbolVa[dataExtern]` to the object's __got slot, dyld fills it at load, and MIR->LIR materializes the object's address by LOADING that slot. A format WITHOUT this field rejects data imports loud at the pre-walker gate — which is exactly the wall rung (2) of the ladder hit — because binding a data symbol through the FUNCTION-import stub machinery would read the 6-byte `FF 25` jump-stub bytes as the object's value.
$artifactProfilesComment: Profiles this format SERVES (plan 06 AP3) — a runnable console executable => cli, the format-side twin of the language's artifactProfiles[]; the driver fails loud `D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch` on a profile not in this set. ★ THE OLD REASON FOR OMITTING IT IS NOW FALSE AND IS RECORDED HERE SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED: the arm64 sibling's comment still says 'macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec deliberately does NOT declare it (its processExit / exit spine is deferred => it cannot emit a runnable cli yet)'. That was true when written; the exit spine (processExit + entryCallingConvention) shipped on THIS file in a later cycle, so the stated blocker is gone and the omission had outlived its reason. MEASURED 2026-08-05: without this key a `--project` build with artifactProfile `cli` dies in ~5 ms at the profile gate, before a single TU is read; with it the same manifest emits the binary. The gate is generic set-membership — a lib/staticlib format declares its own set with zero gate-code change.
$entryCallingConventionComment: sysv_amd64 — ★ MEASURED, and deliberately NOT the arm64 sibling's `apple_arm64`. A verbatim clone of that value is the obvious mistake here and it would fail loud in `injectEntryTrampoline`'s `target.callingConventionByName(ccName)` lookup (src/link/entry_trampoline.cpp — cited BY CONSTRUCT because the line range this comment originally carried had already drifted by the end of the cycle that wrote it), which resolves this string against the TARGET's callingConventions and reports when the name does not exist. THE EVIDENCE, three independent in-tree sites that agree: (1) the ABI catalog pins the row `{ "x86_64", ObjectFormatKind::MachO, CallConv::CcSysV, "sysv_amd64" }` at src/ffi/abi/abi_catalog.cpp:55 — the same file gives arm64+MachO its own `apple_arm64` row at :58, so the two verbs are per-CPU and not interchangeable; (2) src/dss-config/targets/x86_64.target.json:2338 ships a calling convention of exactly this name (SysV AMD64: int args RDI/RSI/RDX/RCX/R8/R9, int return RAX); (3) tests/mir/test_mir_lowering_c.cpp:1127 already pairs `macho64-x86_64-darwin-exec` with `sysv_amd64` in its shipped-row table. Apple's x86_64 ABI IS System V AMD64 — the divergence list that earns arm64 a separate verb (always-stack varargs, indirect-result) has no x86_64 counterpart, so there is no `apple_x86_64` to declare and none was invented. Read via `target.callingConventionByName("sysv_amd64")` at trampoline-build time; the scalar exit call exercises neither the red zone nor the stack-argument rules. Same verb the elf64-x86_64-linux-exec sibling declares — the CPU fixes it, and Linux and Darwin agree because SysV is the ABI on both.
$remainingDeliberateOmissionsComment: ★ WHAT THIS FILE STILL DOES NOT DECLARE, AND WHY EACH ABSENCE IS DELIBERATE RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Written down because the arm64 sibling HAS all of these, which makes the gap look like an unfinished copy. ★★ REWRITTEN 2026-08-05 — THE HEADLINE OF THE PREVIOUS VERSION IS NOW OBSOLETE AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT. That version listed SEVEN omissions and gave ONE governing reason for the important ones: they were 'POLICY deferrals awaiting a macOS-x86_64 RUNTIME WITNESS (this project has none — the operator's Mac is Apple Silicon)'. THE WITNESS EXISTS NOW: the operator's Mac runs a `darwin/arm64 -> arch -x86_64` (Rosetta) launcher for the `macho64-x86_64` leg, declared in real-examples/c/sqlite/legs.json, so a DSS-built x86_64 Mach-O can finally be EXECUTED. Four of the seven rows are therefore DISCHARGED, not merely re-argued — `supportedDataSections` (rodata/data/bss/relro) + their `sections[]` rows, `dataImportBinding`, `artifactProfiles` and `image.codeSignature` all ship above, each with a MEASURED wall that forced it (see $runnableCliClusterComment). The previous version's other load-bearing claim was ALSO right and is worth keeping: the blocker was never missing walker code — the format-blind macho walker emitted correct x86_64 images with the full sibling key set when probed. This cycle re-confirms that from the shipped configs rather than a throwaway copy: MEASURED 2026-08-05, the real upstream sqlite CLI (sqlite3.c + shell.c) compiled + linked to a 4,783,493-byte MH_EXECUTE with 0 errors, carrying `__TEXT,__const` 0x1d960, `__DATA,__data` 0x9890, `__DATA,__bss` 0x4f8, 211 `__got` slots, 6-byte stubs, 4 KiB-strided segments and a verifying 1159-page ad-hoc signature. ★ WHAT GENUINELY REMAINS, each with its CURRENT pinning test re-read on 2026-08-05 (BY NAME, never by line range — the ranges this block used to carry had drifted onto tests asserting the OPPOSITE): (1) `tlsAccess` + the `tdata`/`tbss`/`tvars` kinds and rows — PINNED by tests/link/test_linker.cpp `Linker.TdataItemOnNonOptedInFormatsRejectsAtAcceptsGate` (ASSERT_FALSE(acceptsDataSection(Tdata)) and the same for Tbss on this exact format name). NOT a witness problem any more: it has NO CONSUMER. MEASURED — the staged upstream `sqlite3.c` and `shell.c` contain ZERO `_Thread_local` / `__thread` / `thread_local` occurrences, so shipping TLS here would be declaring a capability nothing exercises. A `_Thread_local` TU still walls loud (`K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport ... declares no tlsAccess block`), which is the correct outcome. (2) `image.segmentPageSize` — its ABSENCE is still the point, and it is now a DELIBERATE re-decision rather than an inherited one: 4096 is already what the absent-key path yields (`kDefaultMachoSegmentPageSize` in src/link/object_format_schema.hpp) and it is the CORRECT x86_64 macOS VM page, so declaring it explicitly would change NO emitted byte while destroying a real guard — tests/link/test_macho_arm64_exit.cpp `MachOArm64Exit.X86DarwinExecDefaultsTo4KSegmentPageSize` is a knob-that-lies test whose subject IS the absent-key path, and an explicit declaration would leave it green while it stopped proving what it was written to prove. Cloning the sibling's 16384 would be doubly wrong: Apple Silicon requires it, x86_64 does not, and it would break validate()'s Mach-O mmap-congruence rule outright, since this file's __text virtualAddress 0x100001000 is 0x1000 above pageZeroSize — congruent under a 4 KiB page and NOT under a 16 KiB one. VERIFIED, not assumed: that test is green with the key still absent. (3) `image.buildVersion` — PINNED by the SAME test as (2) (its second assertion is EXPECT_FALSE(buildVersion.has_value())). ★ THIS ONE IS AN OPEN RISK AND MUST NOT BE READ AS SETTLED. The old justification, 'Intel/Rosetta is lenient', is DOCUMENTED at best and this cycle could not measure it — LC_BUILD_VERSION is how dyld4 identifies a main executable's PLATFORM, and that is an OS-version property, not a CPU one, so the leniency argument may simply not apply on the operator's macOS 26.5. It is NOT shipped here for a concrete reason: `macho::encodeExec` (the STATIC arm) REJECTS a schema carrying `image.buildVersion` LOUD (D-LK10-ENTRY-MACHO-STATIC-BUILD-VERSION), and several walker tests drive this format with zero-extern modules down exactly that arm, so declaring it would turn tests RED for a reason unrelated to the Mac. If the first Rosetta run fails at load with a platform/EBADMACHO-class error, THIS is the first thing to add — it is a three-line block plus that static-arm gap. (4) `librarySynthesis` — the C11 `<threads.h>` shim vehicle; the same no-consumer argument as (1) (sqlite uses pthread directly, and this format ships no TLS anyway). (5) `processArgs` — PINNED by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp `ProcessArgsSubstrate.ShippedMachoExecsDeclareNoneAndPeDeclaresCrtOutParam` for BOTH darwin execs, and CORRECT on the merits: dyld calls an LC_MAIN entry with argc/argv ALREADY in the argument registers, so pass-through IS the mechanism and a stack-vector block would read a stack that holds no argv there.

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity. cputype = CPU_TYPE_X86_64 (0x01000007). cpusubtype = CPU_SUBTYPE_X86_64_ALL (3). filetype = 'execute' (MH_EXECUTE, closed enum). flags = MH_NOUNDEFS (0x1) | MH_DYLDLINK (0x4) | MH_TWOLEVEL (0x80) | MH_PIE (0x200000) = 0x200085 — modern macOS exec convention: no unresolved symbols at link time, uses dyld, two-level namespace lookup, position-independent.

image.$comment: Mach-O image fields for MH_EXECUTE. pageZeroSize = 0x100000000 (4 GiB) — the __PAGEZERO segment placed at vmaddr=0 catches null-pointer derefs at the kernel level. dylinkerPath = '/usr/lib/dyld' — the dynamic linker macOS always uses. loadDylibs = ['/usr/lib/libSystem.B.dylib'] — required for any user-space process (provides start function + libc + Mach traps). Future cycles add Foundation / AppKit / etc. as needed.
image.$codeSignatureComment: D-LK7-ADHOC-CODESIGN-MACHO: an ad-hoc SHA-256 code signature — the walker fills the LC_CODE_SIGNATURE reservation with a real CS_SuperBlob + CodeDirectory (page-hash table over the signed file bytes) instead of zeroes. ★ THIS IS THE KEY MOST LIKELY TO DECIDE WHETHER THE BINARY RUNS AT ALL, so state the evidence grade: macOS refuses to exec a Mach-O whose signature does not verify, and DSS's OWN ad-hoc SuperBlob is what makes a DSS-built Darwin binary pass AMFI — MEASURED on the arm64 sibling, whose signed image ran on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac. The x86_64 side of that is INFERRED until the Rosetta run happens: signing is enforced most strictly on Apple Silicon, and an x86_64 slice executing under Rosetta is being loaded BY that kernel, so shipping the signature is the strictly-safer choice and it costs nothing structurally. The arm64 comment's framing that 'mandatory code signing is an Apple-Silicon kernel rule, not an x86_64 one' is exactly the assumption Rosetta puts in doubt. MEASURED HERE 2026-08-05, the emitted x86_64 image: LC_CODE_SIGNATURE (cmd 0x1D, cmdsize 16) present, SuperBlob magic 0xFADE0CC0, CodeDirectory magic 0xFADE0C02, flags 0x2 = CS_ADHOC, hashType 2 = SHA-256, execSegFlags 1 = CS_EXECSEG_MAIN_BINARY, execSegLimit equal to __TEXT.filesize, codeLimit equal to the signature's own file offset (so every byte before it is covered and nothing trails it), and all 1159 page hashes of the sqlite CLI re-computed and matched byte for byte outside DSS. NO `codeSignatureSize` is declared alongside: the reservation length is DERIVED from this block via `adHocCodeSignatureSize` over the same arguments, and a hand-typed size that disagreed with the built blob is precisely the failure that derivation exists to prevent. `pageSize` 4096 is the conventional code-hash page Apple uses on BOTH architectures and is a DISTINCT knob from the VM segment page (which this format leaves at its 4096 default) — do not conflate them. `identifier` is the CodeDirectory ident string; naming it after the FORMAT rather than any one artifact is the same shipped-schema-identity concession the arm64 sibling and the dylib `installName` record — an artifact wanting its own ident overrides via its own format JSON. ★ ONE MEASURED GAP TO KNOW ABOUT, reported for anchoring: `macho::encode`'s dispatch gate and `encodeExec`'s invariant belt (src/link/format/macho.cpp:751 and :1853) both test `image.codeSignatureSize != 0` ONLY and never look at THIS block, so a zero-extern module would take the STATIC arm and have its signature dropped with no diagnostic. It is unreachable through the shipped pipeline — `processExit` above guarantees an entry trampoline importing `_exit`, hence at least one extern, hence always the dynamic arm — and `MachOCodeSignPlaceholder.StaticPathDropsAdHocCodeSignatureRequest` now pins it as an explicit flip marker.
image.$bindNowComment: Eager binding — the v1 stance per plan 14 §5 risk row, parallel to ELF cycle 2b.2's DF_1_NOW choice. Emits LC_DYLD_INFO_ONLY with the immediate bind_off opcode stream resolved at load via the linker; lazy_bind_off stays zero. Lazy upgrade (lazy_bind opcode stream resolved on first call via dyld_stub_binder) anchored at D-LK6-13; until then, the walker fails loud on bindNow=false.

sections.$comment: __text within __TEXT segment. virtualAddress = 0x100000000 + 0x1000 = 0x100001000 — __TEXT loads immediately after __PAGEZERO at the page boundary. flags (in substrate `type` field) = S_REGULAR (0) | S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS (0x80000000) | S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (0x00000400) = 0x80000400. addrAlign = 16 (x86_64 instruction alignment).
sections.name: __text

sections.$comment: __const within __TEXT — read-only data globals (D-LK3-RODATA, the Mach-O exec read-only data-section arm; the direct mirror of ELF's D-LK1-ELF-EXEC-DATA-SECTIONS). Folded into the R+X __TEXT segment as S_REGULAR with NO write and NO exec attribute — strictly read-only, W^X preserved — which is the same shape the ELF arm's `.rodata`-in-R+X-PT_LOAD gives. `type` is the substrate section flags/type field exactly as in the `__text` row above; S_REGULAR = 0 (plain regular data, no attribute bits). virtualAddress = 0 because __const's VA is COMPUTED by the walker (src/link/format/macho.cpp): it sits after __text + __stubs, whose sizes are not knowable from a static schema. addrAlign = 8 is the schema FLOOR only; the walker raises it to the strictest data item's alignment (MEASURED on the sqlite CLI: the emitted __const row came out align 2^4, raised from this floor). entrySize = 0 (not a fixed-stride table). Segment/section NAMES are arch-independent in Mach-O, so these are the arm64 sibling's verbatim and that IS the authoritative source for them.
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: __data within __DATA — writable initialized globals (D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER). Lives in a SEPARATE writable __DATA segment (maxprot/initprot rw-, VM_PROT 3) placed after __DATA_CONST, NOT in the r-x __TEXT: a store into __TEXT faults, and that is the bug this row's placement avoids. `type` (the section_64.flags field) = S_REGULAR = 0. `relro` items ride HERE too — the exec walker folds a const-with-load-time-relocations global into this section and dyld rebases the slot via the __DATA rebase-opcode stream (see $supportedDataSectionsComment), which is why `supportedDataSections` lists relro but `sections[]` has no relro row. virtualAddress = 0 — walker-COMPUTED from the __DATA segment layout (after __DATA_CONST/__got). addrAlign = 8 is the FLOOR; the walker raises it to the strictest item and writes section_64.align as log2.
sections.name: __data

sections.$comment: __bss within __DATA — zero-init globals (tentative `int g;`). D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER. `type` (section_64.flags) = S_ZEROFILL = 1: the section occupies VM (it contributes to __DATA.vmsize) but stores NO file bytes (section_64.offset = 0, and __DATA.filesize excludes it), and it MUST be the LAST section in __DATA. MEASURED on the sqlite CLI: the emitted __bss row carries size=0x4f8 with off=0x0, and __DATA.filesize (0x9890) covers __data alone while __DATA.vmsize (0xa000) covers both — the S_ZEROFILL contract holding end to end. virtualAddress = 0 — walker-computed (after __data). addrAlign = 8 floor, raised by the walker, written as log2.
sections.name: __bss

relocations.$comment: Mach-O image-side relocs reuse the same kinds as the .o schema (BRANCH/UNSIGNED_8/UNSIGNED_4). cycle-2 walker applies intra-module relocs in-place via the LK6 cycle 1 structured-formula triple; the relocation_info records are NOT emitted for MH_EXECUTE (dyld doesn't read .o-style relocs — it reads LC_DYLD_INFO chained-fixups, which arrive at LK6 cycle 2 paired with FFI). nativeId packs (type<<28)|(length<<25)|(pcrel<<24) — same as the .o schema. r_extern (bit 27) + r_symbolnum (bits 0..23) are walker-filled. ⚠⚠ VALUE CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (D-CONFIG-MACHO-X86_64-EXEC-DYLIB-RELOC-NATIVEID-CONTRADICTS-ITS-OWN-ROW): this row declared nativeId 369098752 = 0x16000000, which under the packing THIS COMMENT ITSELF states -- (type<<28)|(length<<25)|(pcrel<<24) -- decodes to r_type=1 (X86_64_RELOC_SIGNED), r_length=3 (8 bytes), r_pcrel=0. Every one of those three fields contradicts the row's own name and stated intent: BRANCH is r_type=2, 4 bytes, PC-relative. The `-darwin` and `-staticlib` siblings have always carried the correct 620756992 = 0x25000000 = (2<<28)|(2<<25)|(1<<24), and the arm64 family agrees on that same packed value for its own BRANCH26. ⓘ THE DEFECT WAS LATENT, NOT LIVE, AND IT IS WORTH SAYING WHICH: relocation_info records are emitted only by the MH_OBJECT writer, which reads the `-darwin`/`-staticlib` documents, so nothing consumed this number. It is corrected rather than left alone because the exec format serves a real `cli` profile with a real run leg, and a wrong declared value that no consumer reads today is precisely the shape that becomes a silent miscompile the day one does. ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_BRANCH

relocations.$comment: ⚠ VALUE CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (D-CONFIG-MACHO-X86_64-EXEC-DYLIB-RELOC-NATIVEID-CONTRADICTS-ITS-OWN-ROW): declared 33554432 = 0x02000000, which is r_length=1 = TWO bytes, for a row named _4 and (in the dylib sibling) commented "length 2 = 4 bytes". The correct packing is (0<<28)|(2<<25)|(0<<24) = 0x04000000 = 67108864, which is what the `-darwin`/`-staticlib` siblings carry. Same latency as the BRANCH row above: the MH_OBJECT writer is the only consumer of these numbers and it reads a different document.
relocations.name: X86_64_RELOC_UNSIGNED_4
